definition: זֵד adjective insolent, presumptuous : — ׳ ז Prov 21:24 plural זֵדִים Jer 43:2 + 11 t.; — always masculine, and always of opposition to ׳ י , wickedness; with qualified noun expressed, only הָאֲנָשִׁים הַזֵּדִים Jer 43:2 , of opponents of Jeremiah; elsewhere used substantively, as technical term for godless, rebellious men; once singular זֵד יָהִיר לֵץ שְׁמוֺ Prov 21:24 a haughty insolent one, scorner is his name (|| עוֺשֶׂה בְּעֶבְרַת זָדוֺן ); usually plural Isa 13:11 ( ׳ גְּאוֺן ז ; || גַּאֲוַת עָרִיצִים ); Mal 3:13 (|| עשֵֹׁי רִשְׁעָה ), v. Mal 4:19 (|| רִשְׁעָה עשֵֹׁה ); and in Ps 86:14 (|| עָרִיצִים ), Ps 119:21 (|| מִמִּצְוֺתֶיךָ הַשֹּׁגִים ), v Ps 119:51 v Ps 119:69 v Ps 119:78 v Ps 119:85 v Ps 119:122 so probably also Ps 19:14 גַּם מִזֵּדִים חֲשׂךְ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ also from presumptuous men hold back thy servant ( Ew Ol Hup Che RVm ); > presumptuous sins Deal. ( AV RV ).
